title: Normalized derived specialization to a surjective closed fibre section
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p$, a finite norm-topological extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega\supset E$ with its extended norm topology. For $F=E,\Omega$ use the all-continuous condensed ring $C_F(Q)=C(Q,F)$, its pullbacks $C_{F,X}=p_X^*C_F$, internal modules, and ordinary unbounded derived direct images on small pro-etale sites [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site].
Let $q:X\to U$ be a morphism of affine $k$-schemes, $s:Z\hookrightarrow U$ a closed immersion, and $i:Z\to X$ a map with $qi=s$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For every profinite $P$ use the actual test schemes [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects], put $q_P=q\pi_P:X[P]\to U$, and let $i_P:Z[P]\to X[P]$ be induced by $i$. Assume $q_P$ is integral [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and the induced $a_P:Z[P]\to B_P=X[P]\times_U Z$ is a surjective closed immersion for every $P$. Write $h_P:B_P\to X[P]$, $q_{Z,P}:B_P\to Z$, and $\rho_P:Z[P]\to Z$ for the projections.
For a finite-rank lisse $C_{F,X}$-module $\mathcal L$ [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module] set $\mathcal L_P=\pi_P^*\mathcal L$. Define $\theta_{F,P,\mathcal L}$ to be the $\rho_P^*\dashv R\rho_{P,*}$-adjunct of the actual counit pulled back by $i_P$:
$$\rho_P^*s^*Rq_{P,*}\mathcal L_P[0]\cong i_P^*q_P^*Rq_{P,*}\mathcal L_P[0]\xrightarrow{i_P^*\varepsilon}i_P^*\mathcal L_P[0]\cong\rho_P^*i^*\mathcal L[0].$$
Then
$$\theta_{F,P,\mathcal L}:s^*Rq_{P,*}\mathcal L_P[0]\xrightarrow{\sim}R\rho_{P,*}(\rho_P^*i^*\mathcal L[0])$$
is an isomorphism in the derived module category. It equals the cartesian exchange for $(q_P,s)$ followed by $R(q_{Z,P})_*$ of the actual unit for $a_P$, with the canonical derived composition identification. In degree zero it is restriction of full-source sections along $i_P$. For $P=*$ it is the actual boundary restriction $s^*Rq_*\mathcal L[0]\to i^*\mathcal L[0]$, with the adjunction normalization just specified.
These maps are natural in module morphisms, continuous parameter maps, and pro-etale base change of $U$ carrying the displayed diagrams. This includes morphisms of the full-source schemes and compatible module arrows. For profinite families indexed by $Q$ and simultaneous parameter maps $Q\times P'\to P$, the equality is over the entire $Q$-parametrized schemes. The identity, empty parameter, empty $Z$, and zero-module cases are included.
For $C_E\to C_\Omega$ use actual coefficient restriction and the map $\mathcal L_E\to\operatorname{Res}(C_{\Omega,X}\otimes_{C_{E,X}}\mathcal L_E)$, $x\mapsto1\otimes x$ [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map, sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. The two $\theta$ maps commute with this map and the canonical directional derived direct-image/restriction comparisons. More precisely, define the same adjunct $\theta$ for any degree-zero coefficient module, without an invertibility assertion. Its naturality square for $\mathcal L_E\to\operatorname{Res}\mathcal L_\Omega$, followed by the directional restriction square for $\theta_\Omega$, gives the commuting cospan with common source $s^*Rq_{P,*}\operatorname{Res}\mathcal L_{\Omega,P}[0]$ and common boundary target $R\rho_{P,*}(\rho_P^*i^*\operatorname{Res}\mathcal L_\Omega[0])$. No directional restriction map is inverted and no scalar-extension/direct-image isomorphism is asserted.

proof.text: Fix $F,P$ and put $K=\mathcal L_P[0]$, $B=B_P$, $a=a_P$, $h=h_P$, $b=q_{Z,P}$, $r=\rho_P$. All module pullbacks used below are exact. Indeed, [lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport] identifies them, including adjunctions, with section-ring pullbacks. By [lem-sfb-alpha-iso] these are inverse image with the coefficient action relabelled by a ring isomorphism. The underlying abelian inverse image is exact by [lem-sfb-finite-upper-star-exact]. Kernels have the restricted action and cokernels the induced quotient action, so exactness of the underlying sequence is exactness as modules. A finite free basis pulls back to a finite free basis; pulling back a local trivialization therefore makes $\mathcal L_P$ finite-rank lisse. The test construction [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects] makes $X[P]$ affine: it is the fibre product of two affine schemes over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. Thus the integral morphism $q_P$ and closed immersion $s$ satisfy the affine hypotheses of closed base change.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-integral-lisse-closed-base-change] to $q_P,s,\mathcal L_P$. It gives the isomorphism $\beta:s^*Rq_{P,*}K\to Rb_*h^*K$, with transpose exactly $h^*\varepsilon^{q_P}_K$ after the pullback comparison. This applies separately to $C_E$ and $C_\Omega$, using all continuous functions, without a completeness assumption on $\Omega$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: agent expansion of the full integral-source specialization, with adjunction-normalized restriction.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] to $a:Z[P]\hookrightarrow B$ and its empty complementary open immersion. The empty open is quasi-compact, even without Noetherian hypotheses. The module category on the empty site is zero (the empty covering forces its only section group to be zero), so the localization sequence becomes $0\to0\to H\xrightarrow{\eta^a_H}a_*a^*H\to0$. Thus the actual unit is invertible for every module $H$. The stated closed direct image is exact; inverse image is exact by step 1. The actual closed counit is invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-closed-counit]. Use [lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport] to identify all these assertions with the internal module functors and their actual adjunction, for the arbitrary coefficient ring $C_F$. In particular no finite-constant-ring invariance lemma is being applied to $C_F$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: agent expansion of the full integral-source specialization, with adjunction-normalized restriction.

proof.text: Descend the exact closed functors and their unit and counit termwise. Apply [lem-sfb-exact-open-closed-unbounded-calculus] to the exact localization package of step 3, taking both open functors to be zero. It makes the localized actual closed unit invertible on every unbounded complex. By [def-sfb-right-derived-exact], $Ra_*$ is the termwise functor $D(a_*)$ with its canonical computation comparison. Hence $\eta^a:h^*K\to Ra_*a^*h^*K$ is the actual derived unit and is invertible. Apply [lem-sfb-derived-composition-adjunction-normalization] to $a,b,r=ba$ and the ordinary pullback comparison [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp]. It supplies $Rb_*Ra_*\cong Rr_*$ and identifies the derived adjunction with the composite adjunction. The categories are Grothendieck by [lem-sfb-proetale-sheaves-grothendieck] for abelian sheaves and [lem-sfb-modobj-grothendieck] for modules over their ring objects; the sheaf tensor is closed symmetric monoidal and additive by [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed] (with $\mathcal A=\mathrm{Ab}$), hence preserves colimits in either variable. The left adjoints are exact by step 1. Consequently the composite $\gamma= (Rb_*Ra_*\cong Rr_*)\circ Rb_*(\eta^a_{h^*K})\circ\beta$ is invertible.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: agent expansion of the full integral-source specialization, with adjunction-normalized restriction.

proof.text:
Write $A=s^*Rq_{P,*}K$ and $H=h^*K$. Under $r^*=a^*b^*$, the transpose of $\gamma$ is
$$a^*b^*A\xrightarrow{a^*b^*\beta}a^*b^*Rb_*H\xrightarrow{a^*b^*Rb_*\eta^a_H}a^*b^*Rb_*Ra_*a^*H\xrightarrow{a^*\varepsilon^b_{Ra_*a^*H}}a^*Ra_*a^*H\xrightarrow{\varepsilon^a_{a^*H}}a^*H.$$
Naturality of $\varepsilon^b$ changes its middle two arrows into $a^*\eta^a_H\circ a^*\varepsilon^b_H$. The triangle identity $\varepsilon^a_{a^*H}\circ a^*\eta^a_H=1$ leaves $a^*(\varepsilon^b_H\circ b^*\beta)$. By the specified transpose of $\beta$ this equals $a^*h^*\varepsilon^{q_P}_K=i_P^*\varepsilon^{q_P}_K$. Therefore the adjunction bijection [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] identifies $\gamma$ with the defined $\theta$. This proves both its invertibility and the asserted equality of maps, not just an abstract isomorphism of objects.

proof.text: The same adjunct formula defines $\theta$ for every degree-zero coefficient module, with no lisseness or invertibility claim. On $H^0$, right derived direct image of a degree-zero module is ordinary direct image; its counit evaluates a section on a test by restriction. Thus the transpose just computed, and hence $H^0\theta$, is full-source restriction along $i_P$. This can be checked using a nonnegative injective resolution: the degree-zero kernel of its pushed-forward complex is the direct image of the original module, by left exactness, and the induced counit is the ordinary counit. For $P=*$ the test schemes are $X,Z$, $r=1_Z$, and the identity adjunction changes the formula to $s^*Rq_*\mathcal L[0]\to i^*\mathcal L[0]$ given by $i^*\varepsilon^q$, as claimed.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: agent expansion of the full integral-source specialization, with adjunction-normalized restriction.

proof.text: Naturality in module arrows is naturality of the counit followed by the adjunction bijection. More generally let $g:X'\to X$ be a morphism over $U$, with compatible sections, and let $u:g^*K\to K'$ be the supplied module arrow. The full-source arrow $Rq_*K\to Rq'_*K'$ is adjoint to $q'^*Rq_*K\cong g^*q^*Rq_*K\xrightarrow{g^*\varepsilon^q}g^*K\xrightarrow{u}K'$. Pulling this displayed formula along the compatible section yields exactly the composite of the boundary restriction with $i'^*u$. Transposing proves the required full-source square. Composition and identity follow by inserting this formula twice and cancelling the intermediate unit and counit by their triangle identity; the composition comparisons are the conjugates fixed by [lem-sfb-derived-composition-adjunction-normalization]. Continuous parameter maps induce precisely such $g$ by the functorial test construction. Pro-etale base change of $U$ preserves these equations: the exchange $\beta$ has this base-change compatibility by [lem-sfb-integral-lisse-closed-base-change], and the remaining unit and composite-adjunction identities are natural. No base-change invertibility for arbitrary modules is used.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: agent expansion of the full integral-source specialization, with adjunction-normalized restriction.

proof.text: For a profinite family $Q$, perform step 7 over $U[Q]$, using $X[Q\times P]\cong X[P]\times_U U[Q]$ and the analogous identity for $Z,B$. These identities follow from finite-limit preservation [lem-sfb-profinite-to-proetale-finite-limits] and base change in [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects]. A simultaneous map $Q\times P'\to P$ gives the morphism over $Q$ defined by $(q,p')\mapsto(q,\phi(q,p'))$; the equation of step 7 is therefore an equation on the entire $Q$-parametrized schemes, not a test at individual points. The pro-etale base-change compatibility used here is included in [lem-sfb-integral-lisse-closed-base-change]. For the empty parameter or empty $Z$, both target categories on the relevant empty schemes are zero. For zero modules every arrow is the unique zero arrow, and identity parameters give the identity comparison. The constructions above include all these cases without dividing by a rank or choosing a point.

proof.text: Put $r_T=\operatorname{Res}_{C_{E,T}}^{C_{\Omega,T}}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction] through [lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport]. Its adjunct equality says that restricting a counit-adjunct and then taking the forward direct-image comparison equals first using the pullback/restriction comparison and then transposing the restricted counit. Apply this equality to $q_P$ and to $\rho_P$. Since the defining transpose of $\theta_\Omega$ is $i_P^*\varepsilon^{q_P}_\Omega$, the resulting two transposes are the same restricted counit; hence the directional restriction square for $\theta_\Omega$ commutes. This argument uses only the forward comparison arrows; none is inverted. Separately apply the module naturality of step 7 over $C_E$ to the actual arrow $\mathcal L_E\to r_X\mathcal L_\Omega$, $x\mapsto1\otimes x$. Pasting that square with the restriction square just proved gives exactly the stated cospan: both paths start at $s^*Rq_{P,*}r_{X[P]}\mathcal L_{\Omega,P}[0]$ and end at $R\rho_{P,*}\rho_P^*i^*r_X\mathcal L_\Omega[0]$. The intermediate $\theta$ on the restricted module is defined by step 6, without any lisseness requirement. Only ordinary scalar extension of $\mathcal L_E$ is involved; no scalar-extension/direct-image isomorphism enters.
